# Git etiquette

How work moves through this repository. These rules apply to human contributors and AI coding
agents identically — there is no looser variant for agents.

<!-- BRANCH-MODEL:START — regenerated by /project-init only if the branch model was overridden -->
## Branch model

- `main` — always deployable. **Never committed to directly.** Receives merges only from
  `development-Area` (e.g. periodic releases), never directly from a feature branch.
- `development-Area` — integration branch. All feature/fix PRs merge here first. **Never committed
  to directly.**
- `feature/<name>` (or `fix/<name>`) — one branch per piece of work, branched off `development-Area`.

Start work with:

```bash
git checkout development-Area
git pull
git checkout -b feature/<name>
```
<!-- BRANCH-MODEL:END -->

## Commit format

```
type(scope): summary
```

- `type` is one of `feat`, `fix`, `docs`, `chore`, `test`, `refactor`.
- `scope` is the area touched — a directory, module, or subsystem.
- `summary` is imperative and lower-case, no trailing full stop.

Examples:

```
feat(auth): add session refresh on token expiry
docs(build): record the deploy sequence
fix(parser): handle empty input without throwing
```

Commit often. A commit should be one coherent change that leaves the project working.

## Pull requests

- Every change reaches `development-Area` through a pull request. No exceptions, including
  documentation-only changes.
- The PR body says what changed and why, and names anything the reviewer should check by hand.
- **A human reviews every merge.** An agent may open a PR; it may never merge one.

## What "reviewed" means

Read the diff. Run the project's checks. "It compiled" is not a review — someone has to have
looked at what changed and why.
